1.word_for_word: सप्त-षष्टितमे रामो गिरौ रैवतके मदात् । — In the sixty-seventh year, Rama was intoxicated on the mountain Raivataka.; स्वैरं युवतिभिः क्रीडन्न् अवधीद् द्विविदं खलम् ॥ — Playing with the young women at will, he killed the wicked Dvivida.; कालिन्दी-विदारणानन्तरं राम-चरित्रं द्विविद-वधादि-सङ्गतम् अप्य् अनुक्त्वा तत्-पूर्व-भावित्वेन पौण्ड्रक-वधादि निरूप्येदानीं तद् एव प्रस्तौति भूयो\ऽहम् इत्य्-आदिना । — After the tearing of the Kalindi, he does not mention the character of Rama, even if it is connected with the killing of Dvivida, etc., but now he presents the same thing by saying, “I am again.”; राम-चरित्र-श्रवणेच्छायाम् अद्भुत-कर्मत्वं हेतुस् तत्र चानन्तत्वं तत्राप्य् अप्रमेयत्वम् इति ॥१॥ — The reason for the desire to hear the character of Rama is that he performs wonderful deeds and that he is infinite and therefore immeasurable.
1.translation: In the sixty-seventh year, Rama was intoxicated on the mountain Raivataka. Playing with the young women at will, he killed the wicked Dvivida. After the tearing of the Kalindi, he does not mention the character of Rama, even if it is connected with the killing of Dvivida, etc., but now he presents the same thing by saying, “I am again.” The reason for the desire to hear the character of Rama is that he performs wonderful deeds and that he is infinite and therefore immeasurable.

2.word_for_word: नरकस्य सखेति हरिणा वैरे कारणम् । — The reason for the enmity with the deer is that he is a friend of hell.; सुग्रीव-सचिव इति तस्य मन्त्रबलम् । — Sugriva’s secretary is the strength of his mantra.; मैन्दस्य भ्रातेति रामायणे\ऽतिप्रसिद्धत्वेन वीर्याधिक्यम् उक्तम् इति ॥२॥ — He is said to be the brother of Mainda in the Ramayana because of his great prowess
2.translation: The reason for the enmity with the deer is that he is a friend of hell. Sugriva’s secretary is the strength of his mantra. He is said to be the brother of Mainda in the Ramayana because of his great prowess

3.word_for_word: सख्युर् न रकस्यापचितिमानृण्यम् । — A friend does not owe a debt to Raka.; राष्ट्रस्य विप्लवो नाशो यथा भवति तथा पुरादीनदहद् इति ॥३॥ — It burnt down cities and other places in the same way that a nation is destroyed by a revolution.
3.translation: A friend does not owe a debt to Raka. It burnt down cities and other places in the same way that a nation is destroyed by a revolution.

4.word_for_word: किं च क्वचिद् इति । — And what about somewhere else?; कदाचित् स द्विविदः मित्रहा सखिहन्ता ॥४॥ — Sometimes he is a double-minded man who kills friends and kills friends.
4.translation: And what about somewhere else? Sometimes he is a double-minded man who kills friends and kills friends.

5.word_for_word: तस्य समुद्रस्य जलं बाहुभ्याम् उत्क्षिप्य वेलायाः कूले वर्तमानान् देशान् प्लावयामासेति ॥५॥ — He lifted the waters of the ocean with his arms and flooded the countries on the shore.
5.translation: He lifted the waters of the ocean with his arms and flooded the countries on the shore.

6.word_for_word: आश्रमस्थान्वनस् पतीन् भक्त्वा आहवनीयाद्य् अग्निषु मूत्रादि कृतवान् ॥६॥ — Having worshiped the lords of the forests in the hermitage he offered oblations and offered urine and other oblations to the fires
6.translation: Having worshiped the lords of the forests in the hermitage he offered oblations and offered urine and other oblations to the fires

7.word_for_word: अप्य् अधास्पिदधे । — Apy adhaspiddhe.; पेशस्कारी भ्रमरः ॥७-९॥ — The peshaskari beetle.7-9

10.word_for_word: प्रभिन्नं मत्तम् ॥१०-११॥ — I’m drunk with a split.10-1

12.word_for_word: जात्या स्वभावेनैव चापलं यासां ताः ॥१२॥ — Those who are fickle by nature and by nature.
12.translation: Those who are fickle by nature and by nature.

13.word_for_word: हेलयामासाव् अजज्ञे । — Helyamasav gave birth.; निरीक्षतो निरीक्षमाणस्य तम् अनादृत्येत्य् अर्थः ॥१३-१४॥ — This means that he who is looking at Him ignores Him who is looking at Him (13-14).
13.translation: Helyamasav gave birth. This means that he who is looking at Him ignores Him who is looking at Him (13-14).

15.word_for_word: आस्फालयद् योषितां वासांस्याकृष्य पाटितवान् ॥१५॥ — He threw the clothes of the women and tore them to pieces
15.translation: He threw the clothes of the women and tore them to pieces

16.word_for_word: विप्रचक्रे एवम् अपकृतवान् ॥१६॥ — He thus committed an offense in the cycle of brahmins.
16.translation: He thus committed an offense in the cycle of brahmins.

17.word_for_word: शालं वृक्षम् ॥१७॥ — Shalam is a tree.

19.word_for_word: सुनन्देन मुसलेनाहनत् । — Sunanda struck him with a musket.; अहन्न् इत्य् अर्थः । — It means that I am not.; तं वानरम् । — That’s the monkey.; मस्तिष्कं मस्तकावयव-विशेषः ॥१९॥ — The brain is a special organ of the head.
19.translation: Sunanda struck him with a musket. It means that I am not. That’s the monkey. The brain is a special organ of the head.

20.word_for_word: गैरिकया लोहित-धातुना । — Garikaya red-metal.; नानुचिन्तयन्न् अगणयन् ॥२०-२३॥ — They did not think about it and did not count it.20-2
20.translation: Garikaya red-metal. They did not think about it and did not count it.20-2

25.word_for_word: यादवेन्द्रः सङ्कर्षणः क्रुद्धः सन् । — Sankarshana, the lord of the Yadavas, became angry.; जत्रौ कण्ठ-बाहु-मले ॥२५॥ — Jatra, neck, arms and dirt.
25.translation: Sankarshana, the lord of the Yadavas, became angry. Jatra, neck, arms and dirt.

26.word_for_word: टङ्काः सतोयविवराणि तत्-सहितः ॥२६-२७॥ — Tanks with water holes with them (26-27).
26.translation: Tanks with water holes with them (26-27).

28.word_for_word: जगतो व्यतिकरं नाशमावहतीति तथा तम् ॥२८॥ — And so it is that it brings about the destruction of the world.
28.translation: And so it is that it brings about the destruction of the world.
